contentBlocks.text: This week you mastered the Pythagorean theorem four ways. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a² + b² = c² for right triangles (Day 1). Add the squared legs and take the square root to find the hypotenuse (Day 2). Subtract to find a missing leg (Day 3). You solved a real ladder problem (Day 4). Find the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and 12, then explain what real-world scenario this could represent.
Great work this week — you mastered the Pythagorean theorem in both directions and applied it to a real problem! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review the Pythagorean theorem, finding the hypotenuse, finding a leg, and real-world application
Correctly find the hypotenuse of a 5-12 triangle and connect it to a real scenario
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child solve for the 5-12 triangle's hypotenuse.
3. Have the child connect it to a real-world scenario.
4. Complete the review worksheet.
5. Celebrate finishing a full week of Pythagorean-theorem mastery!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often finding a missing leg) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why the Pythagorean theorem only works for right triangles, not any triangle
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four Pythagorean-theorem skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. The square root of 169 is 13. This could represent a ladder problem, a diagonal distance, or any real right-triangle scenario.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 8 Pythagorean-theorem standards (8.G.6/8.G.7) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
